propositions: Review gates currently use partially independent registry, routing, runner, checkpoint, and failure paths leading to policy-ownership defects and inconsistent discovery decisions across code review and plan review.

Implement a unified discovery architecture where both gates derive selection from one immutable effective-policy snapshot containing built-ins, project criteria, routing, prompts, posture, applicability, and digest.
Add `rebar review-plan --retry` command to retry only the latest INDETERMINATE review with retryable missing calls while reusing content-identical successes and granting fresh attempt budget.

Project code-review LLM criteria must require non-empty repository-relative globs; migrate `project.review-phase-boundaries` from empty list to `["**"]` without changing membership and audit all documentation.

The shared discovery executor owns typed outcomes, usage, budget enforcement, and success-only checkpoint mechanics without choosing applicability, truncating inputs, retrying providers, or deciding gate verdicts.

Preserve code review sequential execution, no checkpoints, and topology while moving plan review to digest-complete success-only checkpoint namespace with new versioned typed discovery trace for audit and retry.
